events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Clean Break

options.text: So be it. I will see it done. Now get out of my sight.
Do you think you can speak to the [title] that way? Guards!
You make something of nothing. Go, get some rest, dear.

events.text: [character] stands in your way, blocking the path. "You may not see it, but we are done, we have been for a long while now. Let us part ways before the sheer misery drives us both to madness."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Familiar Face

options.text: [character] is not an easy man to be rid of.

events.text: At last, from atop the throne of [rival], [character] sees you eye to eye.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Free Hand

options.text: Accept [character] suggestions.
Enforce Freedom throughout [family] cities.
The [family] have the right of it. These laws are only holding [rival] back.

events.text: House [family] has been accused of slave-keeping, in direct contradiction of the royal law of Freedom. [character] insists that this misunderstanding could be cleared up simply by some specific "clarifications" of the present law, relating to some specific applications.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Light Touch

options.text: [character] could be very useful to [rival].
[character] reign cannot be allowed to continue.

events.text: It was not an easy task, but [character] has found and infiltrated the [city] house of pleasure favored by [character]. With access this close to [character], there are opportunities for both leverage and assassination.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Refined Palate

options.text: I shall hint at a great surprise.
Just as well he finds a new topic to occupy his conversation...

events.text: Your husband [character] could go on for hours about the distinctions between wines of every region of [rival]. Yet, recently he has seemed almost bored by each new vintage brought to court. But are you not the mighty King of [rival]? Surely you could bring him an exotic taste that would delight even his tongue!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Short Reign

options.text: Prudent rulers must have thick skin.
Impudent buffoons must have a death wish.

events.text: [character], and his supporters, have become one of the most stable fixtures of the [rival] court. So it has become politically, as well as socially, awkward that [character] has taken to making jokes about your height. "... out of reach of even the [rival]? Then I daresay the arms of our little king would need to stretch all the further."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Towering Reputation

options.text: [character] can say what he likes.
I have my limits. [character] has crossed them.

events.text: [character], exemplification of [rival] aptitude, and then exalted ruler... the shadow you cast is long. [character] has at last determined that one way or another he shall escape that shadow. Both publicly and privately, he now questions your decisions and the state of [rival] in general. The hints that his own rulership would right each wrong in turn are none too subtle.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Waning Star

options.text: Such is the passage of time.
I shall yet prove them wrong.

events.text: Many respect you. Others loathe you. But virtually no one in [rival] still sincerely believes that [character] is the king that shall usher in a truly new age of innovation and prosperity.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Waste of Talent

options.text: [character] shall serve as a General.
Let them clamor. [character] cannot be trusted.

events.text: Voices in the court are clamoring for more [character]. They say he has been languishing on the sidelines, when he should be putting his talents to work for [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Waste of Talent

options.text: [character] shall serve as a Governor.
Let them clamor. [character] cannot be trusted.

events.text: Voices in the court are clamoring for more [character]. They say he has been languishing on the sidelines, when he should be putting his talents to work for [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Waste of Talent

options.text: Let them clamor. [character] cannot be trusted.

events.text: Voices in the court are clamoring for more [character]. They say he has been languishing on the sidelines, when he should be putting his talents to work for [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Watchful Eye

options.text: [character] shall rot in the dungeons for this.
[character] shall rot in the ground for this.
... and you just expect me to believe that?

events.text: It is a dramatic entrance. [character] bursting through the door, knocking the cup from your hand, and with a fluid motion pressing his blade to [character] chest. "Please be more careful who you take refreshment with, dear. [character] here just tried to poison you."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Way About Him

options.text: Raise your own hand to trace the curve of his chest.
With a look, firmly push his hand away.

events.text: There is no denying that [character] defection from [rival] has offered considerable advantages. Practically overnight he has risen in the court, and as you have gotten to know the man himself, he has proved no less charming than his reputation. His wry smirk transforms tales that, from anyone else, would be mere overblown bombast into shared jokes and gripping suspense. One night, on a short journey near [city], an evening of drinking and light revelry has dwindled to only you and [character] sharing a fire. After a moment of laughter, a silence drifts between you. You find that lopsided smile directed at you, in full force. His eyes daring, and carefully watching your expression, [character] raises a hand to brush the side of your face.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Accountability

options.text: Come to an arrangement with [character].
Seize the missing funds.
Insist that [character] must do more to help the people of [city].

events.text: It seems [character] has finally pushed his luck too far. Outcries in [city] over levels of taxation have brought royal scrutiny, making it apparent [character] has been siphoning significant funds from the city's coffers.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Among the People

options.text: Nonsense. I'll see to it you will be hailed as a returning hero!
You are really sure?
Oh, don't you worry, you are coming back to court, but not in your old position.

events.text: A tour of [city]'s brothels is proving an excellent day's outing, when abruptly over the curve of a sublimely shaped thigh, a face comes into focus. Is that.. [character]? The one that has been Missing for gods know how long? "What are you, uh..." [character] shifts uncomfortably, and with well practiced cue-taking, everyone else in the room is suddenly elsewhere. "It's... a long story. But, listen, please, don't bring me back to court. All the intrigue, games of status, life and death situations, I just can't." he looks at you, beseeching.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Anything But This

options.text: Grant a divorce.
[rival] cannot afford the distraction of a public divorce.

events.text: [character] is the glorious heir to the [rival] throne. Man of untold wealth, power, and potential. So, one can only imagine how unpleasant he must have been that [character] is so set on divorcing him.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: At Your Service

options.text: I believe I have just the position for that betterment of [rival]. You only need a little patience.
Less niceties it is. You are a rat, [character], and I would die before giving the tiniest shred of [rival] over to your traitorous claws.

events.text: [character] is blunt. "I do not take to idleness well, [title] [character]. And yet, after finally being given a chance to better [rival], now I find myself once again confronting uncertainty and inactivity for months on end. Do not play games with me. If you have no intention of dealing in good faith, please spare the niceties."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: At the Gates

options.text: They want daring and fearless? Fine, I shall issue a challenge to [character]. This matter should be settled properly on the battlefield, no more gutless hit and run raids.
The people of [city] can protest all they like. A cautious approach against these unruly hordes is the only thing keeping the rest of them alive.

events.text: The [tribe] have become bolder with each passing year, and the rumor in [city] is they have been emboldened by your weak hand in military matters. Now the cries of discontent grow even louder as a contingent of local laborers is cut down by [tribe] raiders outside the very gates of [city].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Beauty and Guile

options.text: We should work closer with [character], and her [rival] contacts.
A reputation like [character] makes me uneasy.

events.text: [character] knows people. And people know her. She has contacts throughout [rival] and even [rival]. If any have a bad word to say about [character], you haven't heard it - an impressive feat in and of itself.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Bend or Break

options.text: You cannot hide from your own mind.

events.text: The days begin to blur. Nights bring exhaustion, but not sleep. There is never enough time, yet, somehow, the hours crawl by nonetheless.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Bound By Vows and Blood

options.text: You are [rival] now, [character]. It's time you learned that.

events.text: The war with [rival] has been tearing [character] apart. [character] has a plan to end the fighting that he is certain [character] would accept. He only begs of you to let him negotiate it.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Bound By Vows and Blood

options.text: You are [rival] now, [character]. It's time you learned that.

events.text: The [tribe] war has been tearing [character] apart. [character] has a plan to end the fighting that he is certain [character] would accept. He only begs of you to let him negotiate it.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Burdens

options.text: Perhaps that would be for the best.
It is no use. Duty lies heavy upon me.
You dare try to usurp my power? You shall not get another chance.

events.text: "Darling, does it not seem as if these constant audiences and ceremonies are ever exhausting? Please, allow me to take up some of them, so that you might focus on more freeing pursuits?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Chosen By the Gods

options.text: If the Gods will it, how could I stand in the way?

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: If the Gods truly willed it, how could I possibly stand in the way?

events.text: [character] has spoken. [character] shines with the light of the Gods and is destined to walk their path. Woe upon those that would make an enemy of [character] or [religion].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Clearcut Decision

options.text: I will face these [tribe].
The [tribe] have no power over [character], [title] of the [rival].

events.text: The [tribe] have hunted and worshiped in the forests near [city] since time immemorial. Yet now, within a single season, the [rival] of [city] have felled acre upon acre of land for a wave of new settlers. Angry [tribe] have demanded that you, personally, meet with them to explain the act of sacrilege.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Close Call

options.text: Unnerving.

events.text: The arrow quivers in the wall. Had you not turned at the shout of your guards, it would have cleanly entered the side of your head. The pursuit comes up empty, but the gnawing certainty remains. Someone quite determined wants you dead.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Concession

options.text: We can only keep watch and wait.
Appease the [family] with concessions.
Perhaps a marriage into the royal line will bring stability?

events.text: With every week come more reports of [family] unrest. Trade disputes, minor mutinies, veiled insults in every corner. Rumors swirl of [family] plots against the throne.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Continuity

options.text: [rival] cannot afford a power struggle, and I can see the only path is giving you my blessing.
[rival] cannot afford a power struggle. My apologies, but family is family.
Feign unconsciousness.

events.text: It feels as though with each passing day, the specter of death slides closer to your sickbed. Oh, and look, there is [character], sliding closer as well. "My [title], I beg you once again to reconsider passing the grave responsibility of [rival] governance to the untried [character]. Great crises loom all around us, and it is of the utmost importance that a steady and experienced hand steer us through them."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Continuity

options.text: I think I would feel better leaving [rival] in your capable hands.
Dearest, you overstep.

events.text: As illness shrinks your world to a single room, [character] is at your bedside every day, the very model of a devoted husband. [character] gives your hand a tender squeeze. "I... I worry, dearest. Have you noticed [character] has barely been around at all? And it's hardly because he is busy handling the urgent matters of [rival]! Heaven knows what he is up to, but I am starting to dread how things might fall apart if the worst were to happen."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Contradiction

options.text: Enough. [character] shall learn better. Everyone shall.
Patience. That's the key. Somehow, patience will solve everything?

events.text: [character] contradicts you yet again. It is one more prick, one of a thousand pinpricks of frustrations, the frustrations that lately seem to compose every facet of your life.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Curiosity

options.text: Enter the chambers.
Spy from nearby.
Go on your way.

events.text: Late one night, you pause at the sound of strange noises coming from the direction of [character] chambers.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Delights from Afar

options.text: Confront [character].
Try and ignore the situation.

events.text: [character] has grown fond of presenting [character] with the tales and the exotic delicacies of each of his journeys. Though both try and keep it from their faces, there is no disguising a growing affection.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Detested

options.text: Throw royal support behind [character].
Quietly pave the way for [character] as a successor.
Refuse to interfere.

events.text: [character]'s grasp on power is slipping, at every turn jeering crowds accost him, and even allies have become distant. Rumors swirl of depravity and excess, of pacts with foreign enemies, of dark forces of sorcery. It seems only a matter of time before those disaffected make a move.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Entrusted

options.text: Grant it.
Refuse it.

events.text: These last months have been hard on [character]. He no longer makes the rounds of the ministerial holdings, in fact barely makes the rounds to the dining hall. [character] has stepped in to handle the more active parts of the position, and the two have clearly developed a rapport. As time and exhaustion drag on, [character] has issued a formal request to transfer full formal authority to [character].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Facing [character]

options.text: You misunderstand! Of course this reshuffle was only ever meant to be temporary.

requirements.label: Ruthless / Bloodthirsty
tip: The leader must have one of: Ruthless; Bloodthirsty

options.text: You really do seem to have trouble taking a hint.

events.text: [character] has rarely been one to mince words, and he does not do so now. "Did you really think it would be so easy to shuffle me off as some obedient little husbandsome lowly Governorsome irrelevant Generalsome far-flung Agentan ornamental Ambassadoran unseen Spymastera lackey Chancellorsome retired layabout, after I held the office of Grand Vizier? I promise you, [rival] needs my hand at the wheel, but more than that, you need me, if I'm to turn my influence in support of your reign rather than against it."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Far From the Tree

options.text: Perhaps he must learn virtue the hard way.
[character] doesn't want to take his role seriously? Fine, then [rival] deserves a future ruler that will.

events.text: The rift between you and [character] grows by the day. He has taken to carousing with unbridled abandon, and every lecture about staying on the right path only seems to push him farther down the opposite one.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Glory and Acclaim

options.text: Send a bland royal acknowledgment of [character] victory.
Publicly applaud [character], setting him in charge of military reforms.

events.text: Whether by careful design or happenstance, the victories of [character] have captured the imagination of [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Greater Good

options.text: [character] can fume all he likes.
I have had my own reservations about the future.

events.text: [character] and [character] have never been able to stand each other, but tensions have at last escalated to the point of ultimatums. [character] has told you personally that should [character] take the throne, it would be his moral obligation to thwart such debased rule.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Half a Throne

options.text: You know, I think you make a point.
Please, can we not go into this again?

events.text: "But you don't even like the meetings!" [character] remains absolutely adamant that he assist with [rival] administration. "After all, you like directing those soldiers so much, why not go see to them, and just let me sit down with all those trade ledgers that keep piling up?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Heir of Their Ways

options.text: Perhaps other options should be considered.
[character] will see the error of his ways. Surely?

events.text: [character] has done it again. The exact opposite of every instinct, every instruction you have ever given him. How can someone with this kind of blindness ever be expected to rule [rival]?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Impulsive Goodbye

options.text: I am given to understand these caravans can never get enough asses to carry all the supplies.
...have I gone too far this time?

events.text: You can't help but raise your voice, "That's the last straw, is it? [character], I can show you the last straw! This straw here says you are gone, away, out of the damned palace. In fact, I am loading this straw onto a caravan for you, headed to the farthest reaches of I-give-not-a-damn."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Impulsive Influence

options.text: The great thing about building bridges is discovering what is on the other side of the bridge.
Hold on, is doing this even a good idea?

events.text: [character]! What a surprise seeing him here. You interject in his conversation with [rival] noble. "[character]! How has it been so long! Why don't you come along for my summer retreat to the countryside?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: In the Eyes of the Law

options.text: See that the case is prosecuted.
We should not risk any further antagonism toward the [family].

events.text: [character] of the [family] has proved a thorn in your side over the years, somehow always at the forefront of opposition in every matter at court. But there is an opportunity to see her away from court and away from her position of influence. [character] has not been discreet about her many relationships, and there remain laws demanding exile for the crime of adultery...

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Influence Begets Influence

options.text: [character] does have a way with people, and with governance.
Make clear that the king does not approve.

events.text: [character] has been thoroughly swayed by your influence, bringing him closer... though you are not the only one to benefit from this closer relationship. Now, it seems, the whole court is abuzz with [character] fresh ideas for [rival], all with the implicit approval of the king.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Influence Begets Influence

options.text: [character] does have a way with people, and with governance.
Make clear that the king does not approve.

events.text: [character] has been thoroughly swayed by your influence, bringing him closer... though you are not the only one to benefit from this closer relationship. Now, it seems, the whole court is abuzz with [character] fresh ideas for [rival], all with the implicit approval of the king.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: It Will Be Fun, He Said

options.text: Sigh.
This mood is called responsibility.

events.text: [character] is giving that pouting look. "I just know if you give it a chance, we can work out something to break you out of this mood. Pretty please?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Lending Support

options.text: I don't see how I could refuse.
Refuse.

events.text: Times are tight, and the state of the treasury is... a topic avoided by prudent courtiers. [character] broaches the issue deftly, however. "The [family] have always been the bedrock on which [rival] is built, and we are more than willing to lend out support towards whatever... difficulties recent events have brought. You need only say the word, and I am sure [family] coffers and a team of our most skilled administrators could settle matters in no time at all."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Lex Oppia

options.text: Appoint [character] to administer the laws on luxury.

requirements.label: Female / High Wisdom
tip: The leader must have one of: Female; High Wisdom

options.text: An intriguing idea... and shall we tax the wealth directly, and also apply the law to men such as yourself, [character]?
Argue down [character] and his supporters.

events.text: As the [rival] war looms large, there is a growing faction among the [rival] nobility insisting that to defeat such a foe, luxury must be abandoned and all resources focused on the conflict. Many, such as [character], argue that a proposed law limiting the wealth that women could own and display would not only offer economic benefits but be the moral bedrock of a modest and harmonious society.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Loose Threads

options.text: [character], now there is the firecracker [character] needs to turn him around. See it done.
I will make sure the royal tailors pay him a visit.
[character] sets an example to us all, waste not want not.

events.text: "... and that poor [character], did you see what he was wearing? I could see the loose threads! Honestly, it reflects poorly on the court. Someone should see to [character] wardrobe. Perhaps he just needs a reliable woman in his life?" [character] pauses expectantly.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Man of Confidence

options.text: To deny opportunity is to deny greatness.

events.text: The [rival] war does not concern [character]. Or, rather, he is confident that heeding the [tribe] call for aid, and no doubt easily crushing the [rival], will yield grateful allies and plunder aplenty to finally deal with the [rival] as well. What's more, through sheer wit and enthusiasm, [character] has convinced a substantial segment of the nation of that judgment.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Mercenary Attitude

options.text: We will handle the [rival] without such extorting "allies".
Just pay the scoundrels. Our generals have enough headaches.

events.text: [rival] has come to rely on its Mercenary divisions... a fact that is not lost upon said mercenaries. Leaders among them talk up the "[rival] menace", and demand advance pay, else they might take their swords elsewhere.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Missing Luxury

options.text: The one issue that will rouse them from those comfortable little countryside Estates, it seems.

events.text: [family] nobility have become accustomed to a certain standard of Luxury being supplied to [city]. Appeals to remedy the recent shortfalls remain, for the moment, polite. However, you have no doubt that that tone will escalate if the situation remains unchanged.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Motive and Opportunity

options.text: [character] does seem suited for the post.
I cannot have a man like that anywhere near power.

events.text: Being Spymaster is not the safest of professions. Unexplained death can be, in a broad and unspecific sense, quite reasonably explained. Such has been the fate of [character]. [character] body is not even in the ground before [character] has, quite seamlessly and efficiently, taken over [character] duties. While undoubtedly suspicious it is also, it must be said, undoubtedly convenient.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Opposition

options.text: Avoid him.
Confront him.
Arrest him.

events.text: [character] has positioned himself as the center of opposition to your rule, and slowly but surely his movement gains influence and momentum.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: People Displeaser

options.text: This is not a discussion. [character] will be the next king of [rival].
[character] and I will go out into the nation. We will show them his greatness.
I cannot disagree... [character] would be the prudent choice to lead [rival].

events.text: You never thought you'd see the day. [character] of house [family] nodding in agreement with [character] of house [family]. "With all due respect to [character], he simply cannot be seen as fit to rule [rival]. A ruler cannot simply issue decrees. They must engage with the nation, converse, inspire: in essence, lead."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Playing Politics

options.text: He shows all the hallmarks of a great leader.
I worry these methods take him down the wrong path.
I must tell [character] that this kind of behavior is unacceptable.
With that kind of ambition, he will find a way to the throne, sooner rather than later.

events.text: [character] has not been idle in the role of crown prince of [rival]. The rumors are his friends receive many benefits, and those, like [character], that cross him come to regret it. Exactly which favors, and what retribution, are the subject of the court's most traded gossip.

guaranteed.text: Gain trait: Not Inclined To Marry
Gain trait: Not Inclined To Marry
Gain trait: Not Inclined To Marry
Gain trait: Not Inclined To Marry

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Playing with Fire

options.text: Use this information to demand their loyalty.
See that their rivals know of this.
This situation is too delicate to meddle in.

events.text: The heads of the most powerful houses in [rival], in a secret romance? This was the kind of gossip passed off to the gullible in low street taverns. But your agents assure you, it is true. United, [character] and [character] form an almost unstoppable political force, but just as surely, a whisper of this could set both their houses into chaos.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Power of Prayer

outcomes.label: Power Of Prayer Option O Main
Power Of Prayer Option O Fallback

options.text: I don't think so, [character].

events.text: [rival] stands without a direct descendant to inherit the throne, and [character], among others, has taken keen note of this fact. [character] magnanimously offers introductions to a sect of [religion] devoted to a local fertility goddess of [city]. He assures you that the sacred rites are as effective as they are transcendent and enjoyable.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Rebellion Grows

options.text: I worry where this will lead if we do not act quickly.
This is nothing [rival] has not seen before.

events.text: New recruits join the ranks of rebels in [city], and you can't help but wonder how much farther this supposedly minor insurrection will go.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Restless City

options.text: To dwell on such things is its own folly.
Such a mood can turn in a moment, and when it does, it is best to be known as a friend of the people.
The people need reminding of [rival]'s glories.

events.text: [city] sits uneasy. The streets are full, and the mood is sour. The night breeze carries the indistinct sounds of unchecked tempers to the airy palace balconies.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Rhyme and Reason

options.text: I shall promise him an honored place at court!

events.text: The words [character] produces seem to lay bare the soul of the world. "Or write upon the soul a music that never shall part from your heart of hearts," you quote to yourself. How was his divine talent not seen before this glorious night?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Riches of [city]

options.text: Of course! I shall ready the troops.
Perhaps we can see if they have the good sense to first offer us the finest of their wares?
Doesn't that seem... drastic?

events.text: "But, darling, the mines of [city] are said to be beyond compare! We must have them, and it's not like the feeble [rival] army can stand in the way of our glorious forces!"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Rising Tide

options.text: I can't help but admire the initiative.
If [character] wants to play rebel leader in [rival], then so be it. Send word he no longer has a place in [rival].

events.text: [character] has not been idle. He has not exactly been following orders, either, mind you. [rival] contacts in [city] have been molded into an elite guerrilla fighting force, one giving local governors no end of headaches. Of course, that also means they are no longer providing much in the way of intelligence reports.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Risque

options.text: Praise the art.
Condemn the art.

events.text: [character] has slowly become more bold in his artistic expression. Each recent piece is more transgressive than the last, and the royal court looks to your reaction in order to follow suit.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Rites of Passage

options.text: I will join her in these rituals.
Such a sect is... unseemly.

events.text: [character] has never been one for shows of [religion] faith, but recently she has become publicly involved with a sect of [religion] devoted to a local fertility goddess of [city] and known for their highly intimate sacred rites. Besides being the gossip of the court, the [rival] royal family conducting such brazen pagan rituals has earned few favors from [character] and the [religion] establishment.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Royal Prerogative

options.text: [character] will be [character].
A few words to the right [family] elders could sideline [character] and turn this to our advantage.

events.text: [character] has not been especially discreet in his pursual of [character]. It seems every week the pair find a new hobby to spend evenings in each other's company. [character] is not pleased about his wife's flagrant consorting, but what is he to do against the heir to the throne of [rival]?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Seeding the Initiative

options.text: Grant [character] calls for further projects and reforms.
Freeze [character] out of court.

events.text: Harvest time has come once again... and for the first time in what feels an age, talk is not about how to stretch the meager yield through the lean months. Instead, every minister and peasant is talking of the transformation [character] has wrought in [city], refashioning the region from starving destitution to the breadbasket of [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Seeding the Initiative

options.text: Praise [character] initiatives, and accept calls to name him your successor.
Announce your own initiatives to deal with food shortages.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Sleep Tight

options.text: There is only one prudent course. Rescind [character] charges of treason.
This cannot happen again. Triple the guards and launch an investigation of palace staff.

events.text: You awaken with a hand over your mouth and [character] face staring quite intensely at yours. "I know where you are, how to get to you. Tonight, you live, but I expect to hear word in the coming days that great revelations have cleared my name, and I am a free man of [rival]." You have barely processed the words, let alone a response, as a rush of air signals [character]'s swift departure.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Temperament

options.text: Grant a divorce.
Berate [character] for his actions.
[rival] cannot afford the distraction of a public divorce.

events.text: [character] has not been restrained in his appetites, nor subtle. The rift this has opened between [character] and [character] is no secret, so it comes as little surprise when [character] petitions you for intervention with his wayward husband.

events.text: Time has honed [character] abilities, as well as his taste for power.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Court Schemes

options.text: Keep an eye on [character] political moves.
Console the mourners.

events.text: "Today, we grieve the passing of [character], a lion of [rival] and pillar of our lives." [character] eulogy would almost be moving. At least, were you not aware of the lightning speed with which he had swept in and claimed every one of [character] court duties, powers, and contacts the very moment word of his demise spread.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Die is Cast

outcomes.label: The Die Is Cast Option 0 Main
The Die Is Cast Option 0 Backup

events.text: Last night was a masterpiece of drink, dancing, and dice... probably, from what you remember. You still have the dice, at least.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Favor of

options.text: The thought is intriguing. We may yet make you the [religion] Patriach, [character].
Just what makes you so sure I'd prefer you to old [character], [character]?

events.text: [character] makes many promises. "[religion] is the soul of [rival]. Imagine what can be accomplished with a trusted ally of the king at its head. All that requires is a little well placed aid and support."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Invite

options.text: [character] and [character].
[character] and [character].

events.text: The day approaches. The entertainment has been arranged, the flowers, the dancers, animals the likes of which have never been seen in [rival]. A celebration of the glorious years of [character] reign is at hand, and all that remains is deciding on the most honored guests.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: This Once

options.text: This once, I'll try.
That is not how responsibility works.

events.text: [character] looks upon you with a mixture of pity and sympathy. "You may be [title], but some things are beyond even your power and responsibility. Don't you think, just this once, it would be nice to let problems sort themselves out?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Timely Demise

options.text: Of course I know that. The crown owes you a debt.
It was too far, and you know it. You have forced my hand.

events.text: As [character] funeral procession turns a corner, you find [character] has fallen into step beside you. "[character] had the palace guards already bribed, did you know? There was no other way." He stops abruptly and turns to you. "You do know that, right? It was this, or the fall of everything."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: To Rule is to Disappoint

options.text: The People.

outcomes.label: To Rule Is To Disappoint Spouse Main
To Rule Is To Disappoint Spouse Fallback

options.text: [character].

outcomes.label: To Rule Is To Disappoint Yourself Main
To Rule Is To Disappoint Yourself Fallback
To Rule Is To Disappoint Yourself Fallback2

events.text: A reputation for wisdom, strength, and integrity is a double-edged sword. Day after day, as disillusionment creeps ever deeper, who shall yet taste its sting?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Trapped

options.text: Wait.
I can't just sit here. I will find [character] myself, and I will not be dissuaded.

events.text: Of course he was touring the mine. He was always touring the mines. And now, one weakened support later, [character] is on the other side of heavens know how much rubble, which they can't even start digging through without reinforcing the tunnels to get there.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: What Goes Around

options.text: Give him what he wants.
[character] can say what he wants.

events.text: In his time away from court, [character] has not been idle. Witnesses have been contacted, evidence gathered, priests consulted. A carefully phrased message reaches you that, should [character] exile not be revoked, incontrovertible proof of your many deceptions would find their way swiftly to the court.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: What Have We Here

options.text: Some mediocre offering left by an incompetent, no doubt.
Hmm, let me test the blade's balance.

events.text: You are accustomed to lavish tributes provided by those who seek to use your famously refined tastes as a doorway to royal favor... but something catches your eye among the jewels and finery. An unadorned sword, but seemingly the work of a master craftsman. The strangest part though, setting it apart from everything else, is the lack of note or seal declaring the identity of the benefactor.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Wits' End

options.text: Such confidence. Or desperation.

events.text: [character] has asked, respectfully, about an appointment to prove his abilities- only for it to be snatched away mere months later. He then asked, frankly, if this was mere oversight... only to receive, and then lose, a position in the exact same manner. Perhaps it is unsurprising he has determined that the position of Ruler must also be due for re-evaluation.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Worth More Than Gold

options.text: A price worth paying.
[character] can say what he likes. I will not be threatened.
Cute. He truly has no idea who he's dealing with.

events.text: Perhaps [character] has debts to pay, or perhaps he has simply grown confident. Regardless, he has made it known, discreetly, the price of his continued silence.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Joins The Court

options.text: I have a feeling [character] will go far.

events.text: Our newest Courtier, [character], wastes no time in delving into the sordid dealings of court politics.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Mark

options.text: [character] has never failed me. With his aid, I shall claim vengeance.
My sword has never failed me. With my armies I shall claim vengeance.
The price of vengeance is one I cannot pay.

events.text: Darling [character] is dead. It was poison, [character] says. Some deadly herb, native to [rival]. Causes paralysis, silencing the victim, but death itself is slow and excruciating. You cannot say why [character] has done this, but it seems impossible that he would not have known, would not have nodded to the right person to see it done.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Nemesis

options.text: Sideline [character].
Sideline [character].
Not my problem.

events.text: A few moments of hard stares, smooth escalation to pointed barbs, and arrival at accusations and expletives in a matter of minutes. Some sort of record, frankly, for swift unfolding of court rivalries. Now, of course, comes the tricky business of carrying on with matters at hand, while keeping [character] and [character] at a safe distance from one another.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] The Benevolent

options.text: Publicly praise [character].
Such a demagogue presents a danger to all of [rival].
Send agents to [city]. See if there are other tales of [character] to tell.

events.text: In the streets of his home of [city], rose petals and the cheers of adoring crowds follow [character] wherever he goes. As head of the [family], he has been free with their considerable fortunes, and [character] good works and charity have become legendary. With his name on everyone's lips, the court is abuzz in speculation at the royal reaction.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [city] Booms

options.text: Keep an eye on [city].
Grant [character] even greater administrative powers.

events.text: Under [character] governance, [city] has been enjoying growth and an ever growing sense of prosperity. Whether by careful design or happenstance, the continual successes of [character] have captured the imagination of [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Due

options.text: Defy [rival].

events.text: They say the wealth of the world flows into [city], and it certainly seems as though [character] has been tasked with sending [rival] share.

events.name: [tribe] Families

options.text: Open the gates.
Close the gates.

events.text: As the [rival] [tribe] war escalates, the gates of [city] have become crowded with families fleeing the frontlines.
